es: Discutir los resultados de una encuesta vecinal con cautela: resumir el método, comparar datos, reconocer un límite y proponer un paso siguiente razonado.

teaching.en: The survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood, who were asked about safety, traffic and street lighting.
teaching.es: La encuesta se realizó entre trescientos vecinos del barrio antiguo, a quienes se preguntó por la seguridad, el tráfico y el alumbrado público.
teaching.explanationEs: Método: was conducted + among + muestra; así empieza la discusión de una encuesta.

teaching.es: Aproximadamente un tercio calificó de mal el alumbrado público, mientras que la gran mayoría elogió el parque y su limpieza.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos datos y se usa en medio de la frase, con coma delante.

teaching.en: In light of these figures, better lighting at the crossing should be a top priority for the council, although money is limited.

teaching.explanationEs: In light of + sustantivo introduce la razón; a top priority es la colocación fija para lo más urgente.
segments: In light of these figures, better lighting at the crossing should

teaching.en: Residents are entitled to raise concerns about the sample, because two streets supplied most of the answers.

teaching.explanationEs: Raise concerns (nunca «rise») significa plantear dudas; be entitled to + verbo base expresa un derecho.

teaching.explanationEs: We propose + sustantivo, o propose that + sujeto + should + verbo base; a trial run limita el riesgo de la propuesta.

teaching.en: A proposal is more convincing when it shows that the plan is feasible: a cost, a timetable and someone who is responsible.
teaching.es: Una propuesta convence más cuando muestra que el plan es viable: un coste, un calendario y alguien responsable.
teaching.explanationEs: Feasible significa que se puede hacer en la práctica; los datos concretos hacen creíble la propuesta.

prompt.es: Elige la propuesta redactada con más mesura y detalle.

choices.text: We demand new lamps in every street straight away, whatever the cost.
As a next step, we propose a trial run of brighter lamps.
Brighter lamps will certainly solve every problem in the whole area.

feedback.es: Con dinero limitado y una muestra parcial, lo razonable es una prueba piloto; las otras frases exigen o prometen demasiado.

hint.es: Busca la propuesta que reconoce los límites de los datos.

origin.text: Residents want brighter lamps at the crossing, but money is limited and the survey came mainly from two streets.

prompt.es: Completa: «A la luz de estas cifras, el municipio debería actuar.»

feedback.es: In light of + sustantivo introduce la razón de una decisión: «a la luz de».

origin.text: Nearly everyone asked for better lighting at the crossing. In ___ of these figures, the council should treat the lighting as a top priority.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con la parte que ocupa.

Roughly a third called the lighting poor.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta: el método, un resultado, el límite de los datos y la propuesta de acción.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la concejala ante la propuesta de los vecinos?

choices.text: Supportive, but sure that the survey proves nothing at all.
Hopeful, and confident that a full scheme will be funded next year.
Open to it, but not ready to promise more than a trial.

feedback.es: Agradece la encuesta y toma en serio el problema, pero limita su compromiso a una prueba piloto por el presupuesto; ni dice que la encuesta no pruebe nada ni promete fondos futuros.

origin.text: We thank the residents for their survey, and we take the concern about lighting seriously. However, a third of a sample drawn from two streets is not the whole neighbourhood, and with the budget already committed, a trial run is the most we can promise this year.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué condición puso Carlos para que la obra sea viable.

choices.text: That the cost is not all paid in a single year.
That the lamps go first to the streets where older people live.
That the survey is repeated with two hundred more residents.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que es viable solo si el trabajo se reparte en dos años, es decir, si el coste no se paga todo en un solo año; las otras condiciones no se mencionan.

origin.audio: At the meeting, Carlos summarised the survey: two hundred residents were interviewed, and twice as many older people as young people said that they avoid the park after dark. Sara asked whether the council could afford new lamps. Carlos replied that it was feasible only if the work was spread over two years.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como siguiente paso, proponemos una prueba de tres meses con farolas nuevas.»

answer.text: As a next step we propose a three-month trial with new lamps

feedback.es: As a next step abre la propuesta; we propose + sustantivo la formula con verbo de habla.

prompt.es: Discute la encuesta vecinal: método, resultados, un límite y una propuesta.

answer.text: Last June a survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood. The participants were selected at random from a list and were asked to complete a questionnaire online. Two results stand out. First, roughly a third of the residents said that the street lighting is poor, whereas the vast majority praised the park. Second, twice as many older residents as young ones feel unsafe at night. These findings suggest that lighting may be a top priority for the neighbourhood, and they appear to show that older people are more worried. However, there is an important limitation: most answers came from two streets, and the residents described their own feelings, so the data may be biased. For that reason, we cannot generalise the results to the whole city. As a next step, we propose a three-month trial run of new lamps in the two streets, and we suggest that the council should report the results in the autumn. Further research with a larger sample would then show whether the change really helped, and whether residents in other streets feel the same way.
accepted: Last June a survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood. The participants were selected at random from a list and were asked to complete a questionnaire online. Two results stand out. First, roughly a third of the residents said that the street lighting is poor, whereas the vast majority praised the park. Second, twice as many older residents as young ones feel unsafe at night. These findings suggest that lighting may be a top priority for the neighbourhood, and they appear to show that older people are more worried. However, there is an important limitation: most answers came from two streets, and the residents described their own feelings, so the data may be biased. For that reason, we cannot generalise the results to the whole city. As a next step, we propose a three-month trial run of new lamps in the two streets, and we suggest that the council should report the results in the autumn. Further research with a larger sample would then show whether the change really helped, and whether residents in other streets feel the same way.

We conducted a survey in June, and three hundred residents of the old town answered an online questionnaire. They were chosen at random from a local list. We found two main things. To begin with, about a third of the residents think the street lighting is poor, while the vast majority like the park. In addition, double the number of older people compared with young people feel unsafe when they walk at night. This indicates that better lighting could be a top priority, and it seems that older residents are more concerned. Nevertheless, there is a limitation. Most of the answers came from two streets, and people only reported how they feel, so the results may not be reliable. We therefore cannot say that the same is true for the whole city. Our proposal is a trial run of three months with new lamps in those streets, and we recommend that the council reports the results in the autumn. More research with a larger sample would show whether the trial helped and whether people in other streets feel the same.

feedback.es: El texto resume el método en pasivo, da resultados con proporciones, usa verbos cautos, explica un límite y propone un paso siguiente.

origin.text: Encuesta vecinal (junio): 300 residentes del barrio antiguo, elegidos al azar de una lista, respondieron un cuestionario en línea. Resultados: un tercio (34 %) dice que el alumbrado es malo, mientras que la gran mayoría elogia el parque; el doble de mayores que de jóvenes se siente inseguro por la noche. Límite: respondieron sobre todo vecinos de dos calles y los datos son declarados. Propuesta: una prueba de tres meses con farolas nuevas y un informe del municipio. Escribe unas 180–280 palabras en inglés.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende lograr la carta al admitir que las respuestas vinieron de dos calles?

choices.text: To apologise for a survey that the residents no longer believe in.
To be open about the limits so that the request sounds more credible.
To suggest that the lighting is a problem only in those two streets.

feedback.es: Reconocer el límite con franqueza da credibilidad a la petición; no pretende eximirse de pruebas ni insinúa desacuerdo del resto.

origin.text: Dear Councillor, I write on behalf of the residents of Mill Lane. Our survey, completed by two hundred and forty neighbours, found that nearly a third consider the street lighting poor, whereas most are satisfied with the park. We accept that the answers came mainly from two streets, and we do not claim to speak for the whole neighbourhood. Nevertheless, twice as many residents over sixty as under thirty told us that they no longer walk home after dark. We ask the council to consider a trial run of brighter lamps in our street, and we would be glad to help to monitor the results.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los vecinos pueden plantear dudas sobre si la muestra los representa.»

feedback.es: Raise concerns (o voice/express concerns) es la colocación para plantear dudas de forma explícita.

origin.text: The sample came mainly from two streets. Residents elsewhere may well ___ concerns about whether it speaks for them, and the authors should answer those concerns openly.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué temor expresa uno de los vecinos.

choices.text: That three months is too short to show whether the lamps help.
That the lamps will cost more than the council has said.
That a trial could be used to put off the decision.

feedback.es: El vecino advierte de que una prueba piloto pueda servir de excusa para retrasar la decisión; el sobrecoste lo menciona la funcionaria, no el vecino, y el plazo de tres meses no se cuestiona.

origin.audio: At the next meeting, the council's officer admitted that the survey had been well run but said that the lamps would cost more than expected. She proposed starting with one street and reporting back in three months, so that members could weigh up the results before spending any more. Several residents welcomed the idea, though one warned that a trial might be used as an excuse to delay a decision.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito defiende el autor una prueba piloto?

choices.text: To gather evidence of the effect before committing money.
To protect the council from blame if the lamps prove unpopular.
To prove that the survey's percentages were exaggerated.

feedback.es: Defiende la prueba para obtener pruebas del efecto antes de gastar; no habla de proteger al municipio y reconoce que los vecinos pueden tener razón, así que no refuta las cifras.

origin.text: A survey can tell a council what people say they feel, not what will work. Residents who ask for brighter lamps may well be right; even so, a trial run would show whether fear falls, and that is a better reason to spend public money than a percentage.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los vecinos pueden plantear dudas, pero el plan parece viable.»

answer.text: Residents may raise concerns but the plan seems feasible

feedback.es: May raise concerns admite la duda legítima y but the plan seems feasible la contrarresta.

prompt.es: Completa: «La mayoría elogió el parque, mientras que un tercio criticó el alumbrado.»

feedback.es: Whereas contrasta dos datos de la misma encuesta y va precedido de coma.
